//: The main process is a different runtime from the renderer and gets its own project.
`lib` is ES2022 and nothing else -- deliberately no DOM. A main process that can
see `window`, `document` or `localStorage` is one where a renderer call
typechecks and then throws at runtime, which is the single most common way an
Electron main file goes wrong. Removing the types is what makes the compiler
`module: NodeNext` is what turns `.cts` into `.cjs`, which this package needs:
it is `type: module`, and a sandboxed preload cannot be ESM.
It emits, unlike the renderer project: `dist-electron/main` is what
`package.json`'s `main` points at and what electron-builder packs.
